title: Banco Metropolitano and Banco Promotor Interventions Threaten Systemic Risk
reason: Banco de Guatemala's (the central bank's) own official historical account confirms every material detail: on Feb 9, 2001 the Monetary Board (Junta Monetaria) intervened Banco Empresarial (resolution JM-82-2001); on March 1, 2001 it intervened Banco Metropolitano (JM-112-2001) and Banco Promotor (JM-113-2001) due to liquidity, solvency, and patrimonial-solidity problems; the Monetary Board explicitly authorized contingent credit lines to the intervened banks 'to isolate their problems and minimize potential systemic risk' — matching the description almost verbatim. Separately, on June 7, 2001, the Superintendencia de Bancos took control of Financiera Metropolitana's operations after it suspended payment obligations. Regulators later (Sept/Nov 2001) concluded the three banks (Empresarial, Metropolitano, Promotor) were not financially viable and moved them into judicial liquidation/collective execution proceedings. All actors, dates, causal reasoning, and outcome match the event description.

verifications.reason: Multiple independent Guatemalan sources corroborate all material details. Guatemala's Monetary Board (Junta Monetaria) intervened Banco Empresarial on Feb 9, 2001 via resolution JM-82-2001 (severe administrative irregularities, chronic liquidity problems despite prior emergency Banguat advances). It then administratively intervened Banco Metropolitano and Banco Promotor (the so-called 'twin banks,' both majority-owned by Francisco Alvarado Macdonald) on March 1, 2001 via resolutions JM-112-2001 and JM-113-2001, citing liquidity/solvency problems — confirmed independently by Banco de Guatemala's official history page and by Prensa Libre's detailed retrospective, which gives the negative equity figures (Q764.8M for Metropolitano, Q726.1M for Promotor between Feb-Aug 2001) and confirms the crisis 'could not be corrected' after intervention. Contingent credit lines (líneas de crédito contingente) were confirmed used for the intervened banks in 2001 to address systemic risk concerns, matching the description's 'contingency credit lines to contain potential systemic risk.' On June 7, 2001 the Superintendency of Banks took control of Financiera Metropolitana's operations/assets after it suspended payment of obligations — confirmed via web search of Banguat sources. Regulators ultimately moved the banks toward liquidation: Prensa Libre confirms the Superintendency requested court liquidation of Metropolitano and Promotor on Sept 13, 2001 (resolutions JM-420/421), with permanent closure finalized in 2005 (JM-73-2005/JM-74-2005); Banco Empresarial's liquidation proceeded on a parallel judicial track. All dates, actors, causes, and outcomes in the event description match the historical record precisely — this is a well-known, well-documented episode in Guatemalan banking history sometimes called the 'bancos gemelos' crisis.

Banco de Guatemala's (the central bank's) own official historical account confirms every material detail: on Feb 9, 2001 the Monetary Board (Junta Monetaria) intervened Banco Empresarial (resolution JM-82-2001); on March 1, 2001 it intervened Banco Metropolitano (JM-112-2001) and Banco Promotor (JM-113-2001) due to liquidity, solvency, and patrimonial-solidity problems; the Monetary Board explicitly authorized contingent credit lines to the intervened banks 'to isolate their problems and minimize potential systemic risk' — matching the description almost verbatim. Separately, on June 7, 2001, the Superintendencia de Bancos took control of Financiera Metropolitana's operations after it suspended payment obligations. Regulators later (Sept/Nov 2001) concluded the three banks (Empresarial, Metropolitano, Promotor) were not financially viable and moved them into judicial liquidation/collective execution proceedings. All actors, dates, causal reasoning, and outcome match the event description.
